published_results.claim: No published numbers. "Runs benchmarks on changed packages and uploads results to CodSpeed."
published_results.metric: Run time of langchain-core operations: import time of 12 public import paths (in a subprocess), model.stream with async callback handlers called from sync code, and tool-to-OpenAI schema conversion (warm and cold)
published_results.reproduce_command: make benchmark (in libs/core; runs uv run pytest tests/benchmarks --codspeed)

published_results.claim: No published numbers. "run the create_agent benchmark quickly"
published_results.metric: create_agent instantiation time with a fake chat model, without and with three middlewares (TodoList, ToolRetry, ModelRetry)
published_results.reproduce_command: make benchmark (in libs/langchain_v1; runs uv run --group test pytest tests/benchmarks/test_create_agent.py -m benchmark)

summary: LangChain publishes no quantitative results about its own performance: the root, package and partner READMEs contain no speed, memory, accuracy or cost numbers, and the repo has no docs/ tree or changelog (the bot-generated openwiki/ pages describe the benchmark setup but report no figures). It ships pytest-benchmark/CodSpeed micro-benchmarks for langchain-core (import time, async callbacks, tool-schema conversion) and for create_agent instantiation, which CI uploads to CodSpeed; no results are committed.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
